Base SHA: a18c68be252375a02dbcee6690d2d5de555ef677

(node_modules is symlinked there — do not run npm install). You can also run `git -C /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa diff a18c68be252375a02dbcee6690d2d5de555ef677 f14b549eeae2895ecea49534b5e48ad2c7cdb434 -- <path>` from the main repo to see any file's diff (both SHAs are fetched there).

**What the PR does:** Implements a Zimmermann-branded wishlist auth gate. `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` (organism, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx`) wraps a trigger element via `React.cloneElement`, replacing its `onClick`; if the shopper isn't logged in it opens a `ZimmDrawer` containing `ZimmAuthDrawerContent` (passwordless email/OTP + Apple/Google social sign-in + create-account CTA). All SDK/auth orchestration lives in `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` (286 lines) — the organism itself is meant to be purely presentational. It's wired into `overrides/app/components/header/rightBar/index.tsx` and `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`.

**I ALREADY MEASURED THE GATES MYSELF — do not re-run tsc/lint/vitest/audit:tokens, use these numbers as given:**
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean on both base and head.
- Vitest: base 45 files/689 tests passing → head 48 files/718 tests passing (all pass, no regressions, +3 new test files: zimmAuthDrawerContent/index.test.tsx, zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.test.tsx, useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx).
- ESLint: base 23 problems (5 errors/18 warnings) → head 44 problems (19 errors/25 warnings). I already isolated exactly which findings are new-to-head vs pre-existing baseline noise (don't spend budget re-deriving this):
  - Mostly prettier/formatting noise (trivial, auto-fixable) in: zimmDrawer/index.tsx, zimmSocialButton/index.tsx, zimmTextInput/zimmTextInput.css.ts, zimmAuthDrawerContent/index.test.tsx, zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.test.tsx, useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx.
  - Non-formatting, possibly-substantive NEW findings I have NOT yet assessed for real severity — please investigate these specifically:
    - `zimmTextInput/index.tsx:96` — `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-type-assertion` ("This assertion is unnecessary since it does not change the type of the expression")
    - `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:85` — `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method` ("Avoid referencing unbound methods which may cause unintentional scoping of `this`") — is this a real bug (a method reference that loses `this` when called later) or a false positive?
    - `emailForm.tsx:52` — `@typescript-eslint/no-misused-promises` (async `handleSubmit` passed to `<chakra.form onSubmit>`). I read emailForm.tsx's source already: `handleSubmit` does `await onSubmit()` where `onSubmit` is a caller-supplied prop of type `() => Promise<ApiResult | void> | void`. Trace where `onSubmit` actually comes from in `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` (the real passwordless send-code function) and confirm whether it has its own try/catch so it can never actually reject — if it CAN reject, this is a real unhandled-promise-rejection risk, not just a lint nitpick.
  - `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:255` — I found `'ButtonWithRegistration' is assigned a value but never used` (NEW at head, not present in base). I traced this myself already: the diff removes 3 usages of `ButtonWithRegistration`/`IconButtonWithRegistration` (replaced by `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer`), but the import/binding itself is untouched dead code now. Please just confirm this (quick check of the import line and that zero real references remain) rather than re-deriving it from scratch, and check whether there's a second, similarly-orphaned import in the same file (e.g. `IconButtonWithRegistration`, `withRegistration`, `AuthModal`-related imports that may now also be partially dead).
- `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`: base 1 unacknowledged raw-value violation → head 2. The new one is `zimmAuthDrawerContent.css.ts:58` — `height: '1px', // hairline geometry — intentional px, does not scale with zoom`. This is semantically correct per `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "Units" section (hairline geometry is a legitimate px exception) but doesn't contain the audit script's magic acknowledgment words (`provisional`/`pending`/`placeholder`/`audit-allow:`), so it trips as unacknowledged. Don't re-litigate this one, I've already got it — just don't re-report it as a fresh finding.

**Your job — correctness and regression, specifically:**
1. Read `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` in full (head worktree). Look for logic bugs: race conditions around the two `setTimeout` calls gated by `DRAWER_ANIMATION_DELAY_MS`, the sessionStorage pending-wishlist-intent persist/consume/clear cycle (can it double-fire `onAuthSuccess`? can intent leak across users/sessions if not cleared on failure paths?), the passwordless/social/OTP branching, and the two `unbound-method` and `misused-promises` items flagged above.
2. Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx` — verify the `cloneElement`-based trigger wrapping is sound (does it handle a trigger that already has its own onClick correctly? what happens if `children` isn't a single valid element?).
3. Read the diff for `overrides/app/components/header/rightBar/index.tsx` and `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` (`git diff` command above, or read the full files in the head worktree) — check the actual wiring for regressions to existing wishlist/favourite behaviour, and confirm the `ButtonWithRegistration` dead-import claim.
4. Read the new test files (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx`, `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.test.tsx`, `zimmAuthDrawerContent/index.test.tsx`) — are they testing real behaviour or just asserting mocks called mocks? Flag any test that would pass even if the underlying logic were broken.
5. Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts` and `index.tsx` diffs — this PR replaces ZimmButton's multi-part recipe with a `ZimmButtonLabel` `defineStyleConfig` and swaps `useMultiStyleConfig` for `useStyleConfig`. ZimmButton is used broadly across the codebase (footer, subscribe section, header, etc. per earlier memory). Grep for every other consumer of `ZimmButton` and sanity-check none of them rely on multi-part slots this refactor removed.

Report findings only — file:line, what's wrong, concrete failure scenario. Don't fix anything. Keep it to genuine correctness/regression risk, not style. I'll verify your findings myself before anything gets posted to the PR.

content.text: Let me pin down a few exact line numbers for precise citations before writing up the report.

## Review findings — PR #83 (`feature/SFCC-742_wishlist-loginpanel-content`)

Note on method: no sub-agent dispatch tool was available in this environment (only `Read`/`Bash`), so I ran all five investigation areas myself rather than fanning out — sequentially, but with an actual executed probe (not just reading) for the highest-risk hypothesis.

---

### 1. `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` — logic bugs

**🔴 Must-fix — confirmed double-fire / cross-session leak of `PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_KEY`. CONFIRMED (executed), UNIFORM.**
`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:32` defines the flag; it is set at `:222` and `:243` (inside `onSignInWithApple`/`onSignInWithGoogle`, right before the IDP redirect) but is **only ever cleared in one place**, the effect at `:144-150`, and only when `isRegistered` is true. It is never cleared in either social handler's `catch` block (`:230-233`, `:251-254`), nor in `handleDrawerClose` (`:152-156`). Meanwhile a second, independent effect at `:130-136` fires `onAuthSuccess?.()` whenever `isRegistered` flips true while `isOpen || isOtpAuthOpen` — with no awareness of the flag at all.

I wrote and ran a throwaway Vitest probe (mocking the same dependencies as the PR's own `useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx`, deleted after running — not left in the tree) reproducing: shopper opens the drawer → attempts Apple sign-in → `authorizeIDP.mutateAsync` rejects (network blip, no redirect happens) → flag stays `true` in sessionStorage → shopper instead completes passwordless/OTP successfully → `isRegistered` flips true while `isOpen` is still true.
Result: **`onAuthSuccess` fired 2 times**, `clearSessionJSONItem` fired once. A second probe (fresh mount, already `isRegistered`, leaked flag from an earlier unrelated attempt, **zero clicks**) fired `onAuthSuccess` **once with no user interaction at all**.
Concrete impact via `product-view/index.tsx:558-566`'s `handleWishlistItem` (`onAuthSuccess`), which calls `addToWishlist!(product, variant, quantity)` directly with no idempotency guard visible in this diff: a shopper who tries Apple/Google, hits any transient failure, then logs in any other way gets a double `addToWishlist` call; and — more severely — a shopper who merely navigates to a *different* product later in the same tab session, while already logged in, can get that new product silently added to the wishlist with zero interaction, purely because of a stale flag left by an unrelated earlier attempt on a different page. Whether the backend mutation is itself idempotent is outside this diff's visibility (the real `addToWishlist` implementation lives in a page-level container not touched here) — I can't confirm that half, but the double/spurious *call* itself is proven.
UNIFORM: the same "set on the way out, cleared only on the one happy-path effect" shape applies identically to both `onSignInWithApple` and `onSignInWithGoogle`.

**🔴 Must-fix — "Send code" submit has no loading/disabled guard; double-submission is reachable. CONFIRMED (source trace).**
`UseWishlistAuthDrawerReturn` (`:47-73`) has no `isLoading` field, and nothing in `onSendCode` (`:203-212`) or `handlePasswordlessLogin` (`:169-191`) tracks the mutation's pending state. `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx:65-76` never passes `isLoading` into `<ZimmAuthDrawerContent>`, so `EmailForm`'s `disabled={isLoading}` (`emailForm.tsx:72`) is permanently `false` in the real app — the type/prop plumbing exists end-to-end (`ZimmAuthDrawerContent` → `EmailForm`) but the actual value is never supplied. A shopper double-clicking "Send code" (or clicking again while waiting on a slow network) fires two real `authorizePasswordlessLogin.mutateAsync` calls for the same email.

**🟡 Should-fix — uncancelled `setTimeout` in `onSendCode`. PLAUSIBLE (reasoned, not executed).**
`:209`, `setTimeout(() => setIsOtpAuthOpen(true), DRAWER_ANIMATION_DELAY_MS)` is not tracked/cleared, unlike the properly-cleaned-up focus effect at `:122-126`. If the component unmounts (navigation away) in that 150ms window after a successful send, this still fires against an unmounted tree.

**🟡 Should-fix, re: `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method` on `:85` — this is a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE, not a bug. CONFIRMED.**
`const { formatMessage } = useIntl();` — `formatMessage` is declared via method-shorthand in `@formatjs/intl/src/types.d.ts:64-65`, which is the well-known trigger for this rule on react-intl. I verified at runtime (`node -e` against the real `@formatjs/intl` package in this repo's `node_modules`) that destructuring and calling `formatMessage` standalone works correctly — it does not rely on `this`. Safe to suppress/ignore, not a real defect.

**🔵 Note, re: `@typescript-eslint/no-misused-promises` on `emailForm.tsx:52` — real risk, but narrow and pre-existing upstream, not newly invented by this PR. CONFIRMED via source comparison.**
`handleSubmit` (`emailForm.tsx:33-49`) does `await onSubmit()` (= the hook's `onSendCode`) with no try/catch, passed directly as a native `<form onSubmit>`. `onSendCode` → `handlePasswordlessLogin`'s catch block (`:185-190`) does `(error as Error).message`, which throws if `error` is `null`/`undefined`, escaping the try/catch and rejecting the promise — a genuine unhandled-rejection path, so the lint isn't a pure nitpick here. However: this exact shape (`error.message` in a catch with no defensive guard) is copied near-verbatim from SFCC's own base `login/index.jsx:120` and `checkout/partials/contact-info.jsx:101`. `handleOtpVerification`'s catch (`:197-200`, `(e as {...}).response?.json()`) is if anything *more* defensive than the base equivalents at `node_modules/.../login/index.jsx:130` and `use-auth-modal.js:225` (`e.response?.json()` then `errorData.message` with **no** `?.` on `errorData` at all — base code would throw even more readily). UNIFORM: if this is a real bug, it's a pre-existing one this codebase already ships in the base login modal and one-click checkout, not unique to this PR.

---

### 2. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx` — `cloneElement` soundness

Clean for both current call sites — verified by reading `header/rightBar/index.tsx:341-354` and `product-view/index.tsx:595-610`: neither trigger child carries its own `onClick`.

**🔵 Note — documented but unenforced footgun. PLAUSIBLE, ONE-OFF today.**
`index.tsx:55`, `React.cloneElement(React.Children.only(children), { onClick: handleTriggerClick })` **silently discards** any `onClick` already on the child (cloneElement's new-props object wins), and `React.Children.only` throws a hard render crash if `children` isn't exactly one element. Both are already documented in the prop JSDoc ("Its onClick is replaced... call the original action via onAuthSuccess instead") and are by-design, not oversights — but nothing enforces either at compile time (`children: React.ReactElement` doesn't stop a caller from passing a child with its own `onClick`), and no test in `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.test.tsx` exercises either edge (see §4).

---

### 3. `header/rightBar/index.tsx` / `product-view/index.tsx` diff — wiring + dead-import

**Dead-import claim: CONFIRMED, exactly as described, no second orphan found.**
`product-view/index.tsx:255`, `const ButtonWithRegistration = withRegistration(Button);` has zero remaining references after the diff replaced its one usage (the old wishlist button) with `<ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer>` (`:594-610`). `withRegistration` (import at `:64`) is technically still "used" (to assign the now-dead const), so only the local binding itself is flagged — matches the eslint text precisely.
I checked for a second orphan as asked: none in this file. In `rightBar/index.tsx`, `IconButtonWithRegistration` (`:30`) lost its wishlist usage but **still has a live, real usage** at `:320` (the "My Account" icon for unregistered users) — not dead, not flagged, correctly so.

**Wiring regression check: no functional regression found for the existing wishlist icon/button paths** beyond the hook-level issues in §1 (which apply through both entry points via `onAuthSuccess`/`onWishlistClick` and `onAuthSuccess`/`handleWishlistItem` respectively).

---

### 4. New test files — real coverage vs. mock-checking-mock

`zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.test.tsx` and the render/branch tests in `zimmAuthDrawerContent/index.test.tsx` are legitimately scoped (mock the hook/sub-atoms, assert this component's own render-branch/wiring contract — consistent with `testing.md`'s guidance) — not vacuous.

**🔴 Should-fix (test-coverage gap, not a code bug) — the highest-risk logic in the entire PR has zero test coverage. CONFIRMED via full read + grep.**
Across all three new test files (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx` 234 lines, `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.test.tsx` 166 lines, `zimmAuthDrawerContent/index.test.tsx` 160 lines), I grepped for any test that actually *calls* `handlePasswordlessLogin(`, `handleOtpVerification(`, `onSendCode()`, `onSignInWithApple()`, `onSignInWithGoogle()`, or `onCreateAccount()` as functions, and for any assertion involving `VALIDATION_EMPTY`/`VALIDATION_EMAIL`/`result.error`/`success: false` — **zero matches**. Concretely:
- The double-fire bug in §1 would not be caught — no test opens the drawer *and* has a stale intent flag present simultaneously.
- `handlePasswordlessLogin`/`handleOtpVerification`/the two social handlers could be rewritten to no-ops, or have their try/catch deleted, and none of the 718 passing tests would fail.
- `EmailForm`'s own validation branching (`emailForm.tsx:33-49` — empty-email block, regex-format block, error-message display) has no dedicated test file and is never exercised with an invalid/empty email anywhere in the diff; the one "send code" test in `zimmAuthDrawerContent/index.test.tsx:127-134` always supplies a valid, non-empty email.
- The API-error-surfacing path (`onSendCode` returning `{success:false, error}` → `setValidationError`) is never exercised — `onSendCode` mocks in every test return `undefined`.

---

### 5. `zimmButton.css.ts` / `index.tsx` diff — blast radius

**The premise in the brief does not hold — falsified.** I pulled the full pre-PR files via `git show`, not just the diff hunks (a diff only shows changed regions, so I couldn't rely on it alone to prove a negative). `Button` was **already** a single-part `defineStyleConfig` before this PR (not `createMultiStyleConfigHelpers`), and `zimmButton/index.tsx` never imported or called `useMultiStyleConfig` before this PR either — it rendered via plain `<ChakraButton variant/size>`. There is no multi-part recipe being replaced and no slot removal; `useStyleConfig('ZimmButtonLabel', {})` is a **net-new**, additional single-part recipe for the label `<span>` only, called unconditionally before the `variant === 'icon'` early return (`index.tsx:49`) — correctly placed, no rules-of-hooks violation.

Given that, I checked the change that actually matters for blast radius: `baseStyle`/`variants.primary`/`variants.secondary` are registered globally as Chakra's `Button` recipe, so they apply to *every* `<Button>` in the app, not just `ZimmButton`. I enumerated every real consumer and traced each:
- Grep for `ZimmButton` usage outside this PR's own new files: `zimmTabs/index.tsx:151,158` (variant `icon`, untouched), `zimmDrawer/index.tsx:91,95` (variant `icon`, untouched), `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx:98-99` (variant `secondary` **and** `primary` — the two variants that did change).
- Grep for raw `<Button variant="primary"|"secondary">` bypassing `ZimmButton` entirely: only the two inside this PR's own `emailForm.tsx`/`createAccount.tsx` (via `ZimmButton`, already accounted for) — no other direct consumer exists.
- `primary`'s border removal (`zimmButton.css.ts` diff, `-border/-borderColor` on `:46-56`): the border colour always matched the fill colour in every prior state (bg==borderColor in default/hover/active/disabled), so the border was already invisible — removing it is a genuine no-op, CONFIRMED harmless everywhere.

This **is** a real semantic change. Its one live consumer, `ZimmSubscribeModal`'s "Cancel" button, sits on `ZimmModal`'s own panel background, which I confirmed is also `var(--zimm-color-bg-07)` — so today it's visually a no-op by coincidence. **🟡 Should-fix/note, PLAUSIBLE for future consumers, ONE-OFF today**: any future `secondary` ZimmButton placed over a non-white surface would silently regress, since the two values are no longer interchangeable even though they render the same today.
- The new `baseStyle` additions (`display:inline-flex`, `gap: var(--zimm-scale-2xs)`, `overflow:clip`) apply to every `<Button>`/`<IconButton>` app-wide. I checked the only two raw multi-child `<Button variant="unstyled">` usages in the touched files (`rightBar/index.tsx:181` "Close" control, `:307` "Log out") against their own `__css` styles (`rightBar.css.ts`): `closeControl` already defines its own explicit `gap` (which wins over baseStyle), and the "Log out" button's inner spacing lives on a nested `<chakra.div>` (a different element, not the `<Button>` itself, so the Button's own new `gap` has no children to act on).
